components.note: First-listed current official period5 elective, selected independently ofUCRfit; Year2Finance precedes it.

components.name: International exchange semester
components.note: Mandatory international exchange semester at one of more than 150 partner universities on six continents; the credits are earned abroad and the specific course content is not fixed by the VU curriculum.

components.name: Foundations of Strategic Management
components.note: Strategy and Organization specialization course, period 4 (E_IBK3_FSM, 6 EC, level 300). It examines the classical and contemporary debates of strategic management and requires a real-life strategic case analysis. The course page lists the compulsory IBA courses Organization Theory, Academic Skills, International Strategy and Business Research Methods - Quantitative as recommended background; all four precede it in this pathway.

components.name: Strategic Management from a Practice Perspective: A Day in the Life of a CEO
components.note: Strategy and Organization specialization course, period 5 (E_IBK3_SMPP, 6 EC, level 300). Students act as an executive board and produce a strategic plan covering context analysis, competitive strategy and business model, and corporate strategy. The course page lists Organization Theory, Academic Skills, International Strategy and Foundations of Strategic Management as recommended background; all precede it in this pathway.

components.name: Bachelor's thesis (Strategy and Organization)
components.note: Individual 12-EC thesis (E_IBA3_THESI) on an international business topic within the Strategy and Organization specialization, written as a systematic literature review or an empirical study. Students who have not passed Academic Skills, Business Research Methods - Qualitative and Business Research Methods - Quantitative cannot start it; all three precede it in this pathway, and the two specialization courses are its recommended background.

Retain three qualified responses after actual content/weight challenge. Primary retains all24sound courses:17BENcourses127.5EC including two gateways, economics, venture development, digital strategy, marketing/research, international business governance/law, organisational leadership and finance. These are actual taught business objects and methods, not a generic coherent social-science programme. Second replaces the inorganic-chemistry/materials sequence with actual digital strategy and multivariate research, leaving14BENcourses105EC and37.5ECenvironmental/social-sustainability enquiry; LCA, climate and public governance inform corporate responsibility without becoming logistics or sustainable-finance theory. Third removes literary stylistics and civil-society theory in favour of accounting and finance, retaining15BENcourses112.5EC alongside consumer psychology, empirical/data skills, product development and rhetorical communication. Cultural and sociological companions do not provide systematic regional or cross-cultural marketing training. Sustained marketing/business work supports the qualified international-market question. Different organising priorities produce6/7/10exclusivecourses each way (45/52.5/75EC); distinctness is substantive as well as numerical. None supplies VU business-mathematics sequence, supply-chain/process management, enterprise information systems, dedicated advanced corporate-strategy sequence, compulsory exchange or individual thesis. AIbusiness/ethics analysis does not promise identical appliedGenAItool training. This retains target-defining business substance while leaving major specialist/institutional differences explicit.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic International Business Administration bachelor, and the adopted 2026-2027 programme schedule requires one of eleven year-3 specializations, each fixing two 6-EC courses and the subject of the 12-EC thesis, so one must be instantiated. The regulations define the programme as international business administration and state that it prepares students for a subsequent master's in Business Administration or Entrepreneurship; its compulsory core includes Organization Theory, International Strategy and Business Processes. Accounting, Economics, Finance, Financial Management, Marketing, Strategic Human Resource Management / Leadership and Change Management, Digital Business Innovation and Transport and Supply Chain Management each deepen one functional discipline, while Entrepreneurship and Management Consulting apply strategy to a particular setting. Strategy and Organization is the general-management specialization of business administration: both of its courses list the compulsory Organization Theory and International Strategy courses as recommended background, and Foundations of Strategic Management is also the shared first course of the Entrepreneurship and Management Consulting specializations. It therefore best represents the programme's broad business-administration identity. The choice was made from the official evidence alone and does not improve the UCR match: both specialization rows and the thesis remain without a UCR counterpart.

basisLabels: International business administration: how firms are organised, managed and operated across borders
courseTraceability.rationale: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations Experiential venture development, market validation and business planning give substantive enterprise decision-making practice; not the same manufacturing-process bootcamp as VU BusinessProcesses.. It implements the explicit academic basis “International business administration: how firms are organised, managed and operated across borders”.

basisLabels: Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Economics teaches the micro- and macroeconomic principles the programme's global-economics strand depends on, from consumer and firm theory and market structure to aggregate output, unemployment, inflation and the short-run behaviour of goods and financial markets. It implements the explicit academic basis “Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy”.

basisLabels: Legal frameworks governing cross-border business
courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice sets out the legal systems, constitutional, administrative, criminal, international, property, contract and tort law that a cross-border business curriculum presupposes, and practises them through case law and trial simulations. It implements the explicit academic basis “Legal frameworks governing cross-border business”.

basisLabels: Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project
courseTraceability.rationale: Research Methods & Statistics delivers the research-design and statistics training the programme requires, covering operationalization, sampling, experimental design, survey and laboratory research and descriptive and inferential statistics up to analysis of variance. It implements the explicit academic basis “Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project”.

basisLabels: International strategy, digital technologies and the responsible use of AI in business
courseTraceability.rationale: Strategy & Digital Transformation develops a strategic plan from vision to execution and analyses how digital technology change reshapes strategy, business models and corporate social responsibility. It implements the explicit academic basis “International strategy, digital technologies and the responsible use of AI in business”.

basisLabels: Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business
courseTraceability.rationale: Ethics works through virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism and applies them to practical questions of equality, poverty and wealth, future generations and climate change, which partially supports the moral-reasoning training behind the programme's compulsory ethics course. It implements the explicit academic basis “Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business”.

basisLabels: Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project
courseTraceability.rationale: Qualitative Research Methodology Actual qualitative research design, collection, interpretation and team enquiry provide partial methods correspondence in a societal setting, rather than an identical business project.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project”.

basisLabels: Accounting, corporate finance and financial decision-making
courseTraceability.rationale: Accounting & Corporate Finance Financial statements and annual-report analysis supply actual accounting training. Additional corporate-finance content is not inferred solely from the course title.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Accounting, corporate finance and financial decision-making”.

basisLabels: Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy
courseTraceability.rationale: International Macroeconomics analyses national income, growth, inflation and unemployment, the effect of fiscal and monetary policy, business cycles, economic crises and international trade, the macroeconomic material behind the programme's economics in a global era. It implements the explicit academic basis “Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy”.

basisLabels: People in business and society: organisational behaviour, leadership and the management of diverse teams
courseTraceability.rationale: Personal Leadership introduces leadership theory with an emphasis on self-awareness, goal-setting and emotional intelligence, the personal-leadership foundation on which the programme's people-in-business strand builds. basisLabels: Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Partial curricular relationship. Both address the core academic skills of selecting and critically analysing sources, articulating research questions and arguments and writing and presenting academically. The UCR course adds personal and civic development and community engagement, which the VU course does not.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address the statistics a business student needs, from descriptive measures to inferential testing, together with the research design in which they are used. The UCR course combines methodology and statistics in one course rather than separating them.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address the quantitative analysis used in empirical research on people, including regression, analysis of variance and further multivariate models. The UCR course is set in the health and behavioural sciences rather than in business.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address qualitative research: design, data collection and management, interpretation of meaning and dissemination. The VU course applies this to business questions; the UCR course applies it to social processes.

Partial curricular relationship. Both require students to integrate evidence in a complete empirical research project: designing it, collecting and analysing data and reporting the result. The VU project is discipline-general, while the UCR course carries out that project as market research.

UCR offers no business mathematics course. Mathematical Methods exists in the Data Science & Intelligent Systems cluster but is not part of any of these three programmes, and no scheduled course teaches calculus, algebra or mathematical modelling for business, so the row stays blank rather than being filled with a statistics course.

The 12-EC bachelor's thesis, written on an international business topic within the Strategy and Organization specialization, has no counterpart among the 24 scheduled UCR courses: none of these programmes contains a thesis. Independent research appears instead as the standardized optional 15-EC comparison element shown alongside this component.

Partial curricular relationship. Both concern managing people, and both treat cultural and individual difference as the central practical problem of doing so. The VU course builds that on psychological foundations, while the UCR course works from leadership theory and diversity management.

Partial curricular relationship. Both examine how organisations work: structure, culture, motivation, group dynamics, power and decision-making. The VU course approaches this as organisation theory, while the UCR course works from organisational psychology and behaviour, so it covers the behavioural half of the subject at 300 level rather than the theory of organisational design as such.

No scheduled UCR course teaches the design, management and improvement of business processes. Consumer Product Design covers one product-development process and Strategy & Digital Transformation covers business-model change, but neither addresses business-process management as a subject, so the row stays blank.

No sufficiently direct scheduled counterpart established: enterprise information systems and intercultural strategic business situations are not replaced by general data handling or social psychology.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address economic principles as the foundation of the programme, covering consumer and firm behaviour, market structure and the main macroeconomic aggregates. The VU course frames those principles for a global era, a framing the UCR programmes carry in International Macroeconomics.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on reading and analysing financial statements and annual reports. No additional corporate-finance content is inferred from the UCR title.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address financial decision-making: analysing financial data, assessing risk and making investment, budgeting and funding decisions. The UCR course is a 300-level case-based course that also covers money and banking.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address strategy formation, from analysis and vision through to execution, and both examine how business models change. The VU course frames strategy internationally, while the UCR course frames it around digital transformation; the international dimension is carried separately by International Business & Governance.

Partial curricular relationship. Both study marketing strategy and what drives consumer behaviour and engagement with brands. The VU course foregrounds cultural difference across markets, while the UCR course foregrounds consumer psychology, brand strategy and digital and AI-driven marketing.

UCR teaches no supply-chain management. Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation examine material flows for their environmental impact, not the planning, sourcing and logistics of a global supply chain, so no scheduled UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart and the row stays blank.

Partial curricular relationship. Both establish what sustainability means and which planetary limits economic activity operates within, as a first-year foundation for later sustainability work. The VU course does so from a business perspective; the UCR gateway course does so from sustainability science.

Partial curricular relationship. Both address dedicated ethics courses that teach the main normative theories and then apply them to contested practical questions. The VU course applies them to business, while the UCR course applies them to equality, poverty, future generations and climate change.

No sufficiently direct scheduled counterpart established: enterprise information systems and intercultural strategic business situations are not replaced by general data handling or social psychology.
Selected restricted elective examines corporate accountability, financial/non-financial reporting, carbon accounting, budgeting and control. No scheduled UCR course reproduces this complete syllabus.
Selected restricted elective examines capital structure, valuation and sustainable corporate finance. General financial decisions and environmental context do not replace it.

Foundations of Strategic Management is the period-4 course of the instantiated Strategy and Organization specialization. It is not matched to a UCR course: Strategy & Digital Transformation, the only strategy course in these programmes, is already matched to the compulsory International Strategy course, and no other scheduled UCR course studies the debates of strategic management at this depth.

Strategic Management from a Practice Perspective is the period-5 course of the instantiated Strategy and Organization specialization. It is not matched to a UCR course: no further scheduled UCR course asks students to build a firm-level strategic plan from the position of a chief executive, so the row keeps its full 6 EC on the VU side and stays blank on the UCR side.

The mandatory 30-EC exchange semester has no counterpart in these UCR programmes. UCR students may study abroad, but no exchange component is part of the 180 EC reconstructed here, so the row keeps its full 30 EC on the VU side and stays blank on the UCR side.

notes.text: These alternatives retain substantial business study, with different sustainability or consumer-facing companions. VU additionally requires business mathematics, specialist operations and supply-chain management, enterprise information systems, a mandatory exchange and an advanced specialisation with an individual thesis. UCR environmental science does not replace logistics or sustainable finance; general data skills do not replace information-systems management. Optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

VU combines compulsory 6 EC units, two restricted electives, an approved 30 EC exchange and a specialisation with a thesis. These UCR schedules each contain 24 courses of 7.5 EC, arranged four per semester. They provide related business education through a different structure, with the specialist and experiential differences shown here.
